motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Chad Decoursey for Planning Commission for a one -year vacated term…
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to approve the appointment of Chad Decoursey for Planning Commission for a one -year vacated term beginning May 2026 t hrough March 202 7. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Chad Decoursey joins the Planning Commission
motions.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey to fill a vacated Planning Commission seat, a roughly one-year term running from May 2026 through March 2027.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents right away, though the Planning Commission is the board that reviews zoning and new development before it reaches the council.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Laura Jensen for Planning Commission Alternate for a three -year ter…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Laura Jensen for Planning Commission Alternate for a three -year term beginning May 2026 through March 2029. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Laura Jensen named Planning Commission alternate
motions.summary: The council appointed Laura Jensen as an alternate on the Planning Commission for a three-year term running from May 2026 to March 2029.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Alternates step in when a regular commissioner is absent from the board that reviews zoning and development proposals.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda , including correcting a typo in Item 14.A. to reflect 2026 -2027 and removing Item 14.B. for placement under Scheduled Items on the current agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda of grouped items, correcting a typo to read 2026-2027 and pulling one item out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It's the single batch vote that clears uncontested items in one go.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement with Ivory Homes.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement with Ivory Homes with the following amendments in section (e): • Revise the language from “will” to “may” in the sentence, “The City may consider providing benefits to the Developer… ”; and • Remove subsection (i) “reduced water requirements per lot .” Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ivory Homes agreement approved, water break cut
motions.summary: The city approved an agreement with builder Ivory Homes but removed a proposed break on per-lot water requirements and downgraded promised city benefits to something it "may" consider.
motions.impact: Ivory Homes will have to meet the city's normal water requirement for each lot rather than a reduced one, and any city incentives are now optional rather than guaranteed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10.030 Definitions and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10.030 Definitions and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change to home-building rules rejected
motions.summary: The council turned down a proposed change to the city's definitions and residential development standards, leaving the current rules for building homes in place.
motions.impact: Nothing changes — the rules governing what can be built on residential lots stay as they are, and builders and homeowners keep working under the existing standards.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Flagship Homes Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Flagship Homes Development Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development agreement with Flagship Homes approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with homebuilder Flagship Homes; the motion itself names no location, acreage, or number of homes.
motions.impact: A development agreement locks in the terms a builder must follow before it breaks ground. The motion doesn't say where this project sits or how many homes it covers, so the effect on any one neighborhood is unclear.

motions.item_title: Add pricing of concreate forms to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to add pricing of concreate forms to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Add concrete form pricing to the priorities list
motions.summary: The council added the pricing of concrete forms to the city's legislative priorities list for staff to look into.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this just flags a topic for future discussion, with no decision or cost attached to it yet.

motions.item_title: Add to the Legislative Priorities List a direction for staff to work with the City Council to d…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add to the Legislative Priorities List a direction for staff to work with the City Council to develop a policy regarding paper water rights and prioritization dates. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Study a policy on paper water rights
motions.summary: The council directed staff to work with them on a policy covering paper water rights and priority dates, adding it to the city's legislative priorities list.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only puts the topic on the city's to-do list. Any actual water rights policy would have to come back to the council later.
